$comment: Near AI OS Design System token source. Edit this file, then run `make build` (scripts/build.py) to regenerate every file in dist/, and `make check` to hold the contrast floors. Values are pinned: product accents and increased-contrast inks were solved once with scripts/accent.py and the worst-case ground model, then written here.
name: Near AI OS Design System

contrast.note: Glass shows whatever is behind it, so text is measured over the worst desktop: white under dark glass, #333333 under light glass. A ground is built bottom-up: desktop, glass-veil, pane-fill, then the tier fill.

scene.usage: The ground behind a window or page: the desktop stand-in on web and the first-run backdrop. Never under text.

scene-warm.usage: The lighter center of the scene gradient (radial, scene-warm to scene).

scene-glow-1.usage: Web scene glow, top left (radial). Decorative; never under text without a pane.

scene-glow-2.usage: Web scene glow, bottom right. Decorative.

scene-glow-brand.usage: The one brand glow drawn straight on the scene: the welcome glow rising behind a composer, the first-run corner glow. Near AI blue at low alpha; never under body text without a card.

scene-card.usage: A card drawn straight on the scene with no pane under it: the first-run stage's settings card, a welcome screen's card.

scene-control.usage: A neutral control drawn straight on the scene (first-run Back). Lighter than `control`, whose dark well vanishes on the navy scene.

scene-rule.usage: A rule or dashed line drawn straight on the scene, stronger than `rule`.

glass-veil.usage: The tint painted over a pane's native material (or over backdrop blur on web) so text holds 4.5:1 over any desktop. Navigation layer only.

pane-fill.usage: The flat fill painted over the veil on every pane.

pane-base.usage: A pane where no native material or blur exists (modal backing, Android and Windows panes).

pane-opaque.usage: A pane under Reduce Transparency, forced colors or low-power mode: solid. Also the chart and the reference ground for status marks.

card.usage: A card on a pane (painted, never blurred).

card-quiet.usage: A quiet card: inspector sections, menus inside panels, notices.

card-hover.usage: Replaces the card fill under the pointer on an interactive card.

card-on-opaque.usage: A card on an opaque ground (pane-base, pane-opaque): phone and tablet screens, Reduce Transparency, opaque content panes. In dark the glass card matches the opaque pane and would vanish.

card-quiet-on-opaque.usage: A quiet card on an opaque ground.

card-nested.usage: A card drawn on a card: the inner container that holds a detail or an estimate inside a card. One step from the card it sits on; never a third level.

control.usage: The neutral (glass) button, picker and toolbar-group fill.

control-hover.usage: Replaces the control fill under the pointer.

control-on-menu.usage: A neutral control or pill drawn on a menu, popover or other floating surface, where `control` would vanish into the floating fill.

control-on-selection.usage: A neutral control or pill drawn on a selected row (`selection`). Its label and glyph take `text-on-accent`.

well.usage: A recessed track: segmented-control track, legend cell, unchecked checkbox.

field.usage: A text field, text area or select well.

consent.usage: The consent block and code block ground.

popover.usage: A popover, node card or tooltip on the floating layer (over its own blur). 94%: opaque enough that rows and pills under it never show through (owner, 2026-10-05 web and 2026-10-19 macOS).

menu.usage: A menu or dropdown on the floating layer (over its own blur). 94%, for the same reason as `popover`.

scrim-modal.usage: Behind a modal, over an 8px blur of the window content.

inactive-dim.usage: Painted over a pane when its window is not key, so background windows read darker.

hairline.usage: One device pixel between rows inside a list or table. Never around a container.

rule.usage: Under a modal header, over its footer, under tab rows, and section rules.

edge-hc.usage: The 1pt solid edge every painted surface gets under increased contrast.

row-hover.usage: Replaces an unselected row's fill under the pointer. Never over a selected row.

toggle-off.usage: The 16 to 18% ink behind things that are off or empty: a progress track, the spinner ring, the subtle badge. The switch track uses `toggle-track-off`.

toggle-track-off.usage: A switch track when off. In the dark themes it is 38% white so the navy off knob (`toggle-knob-off`) holds 3:1 on it (owner, 2026-10-22).

toggle-knob-off.usage: A switch knob when off. White in the light themes; in the dark themes the same navy as the on knob (`text-on-accent`), so on and off differ by track and position, not by knob.

toolbar-glyph-off.usage: A toolbar glyph whose pane is hidden (3:1 on the control).

toolbar-expanded.usage: A toolbar button whose menu is open.

text-primary.usage: Titles, body and values on every pane, card, field, popover and menu.

text-secondary.usage: Supporting lines, labels, inactive tabs. Same grounds as text-primary.

text-tertiary.usage: Captions, eyebrows, axis labels, timestamps. Same grounds as text-primary.

text-placeholder.usage: A field's prompt. Text, so it holds 4.5:1 on field.

text-placeholder-on-opaque.usage: Placeholder text on an opaque ground (`pane-opaque`, `card-on-opaque`, phone and web shells with no glass). Quieter than `text-placeholder`, which is already at the 4.5:1 floor over the worst glass ground. Never on glass.

accent.usage: The one action and every selected state: primary button, selected segment and row, switch on, checkbox on, radio on. Holds 3:1 against every ground.

accent-pressed.usage: The accent fill while pressed (8% darker, never a fade).

text-on-accent.usage: Labels and glyphs on accent, accent-pressed and menu-hover.

accent-text.usage: Links, accent eyebrows and accent text on every ground text-primary uses.

accent-soft.usage: Accent marks that are not text: series, step-progress nodes, tab ember, promo edges. 3:1 on pane-opaque.

accent-tint.usage: A tinted background behind accent content (accent tags, the selected filter chip ground).

tab-ember.usage: The 2pt line under the selected main tab, fading at both ends.

tab-ember-halo.usage: The glow rising from the tab ember behind the selected title.

focus-ring.usage: The 2px keyboard focus ring, 2px outside the control. 3:1 against every ground.

selection.usage: A selected list or table row (with text-on-accent).

positive.usage: Positive status mark (dot, glyph): on, watching, verified. Always beside words.

positive-text.usage: Positive status as text, on every ground and on positive-tint.

positive-tint.usage: Positive tag ground. A notice never takes a tint; its tone is the dot in its title.

proof-text.usage: The word of a passed proof (Verified) and the seal's ink, on `proof-tint`. Calmer than `positive-text` so a proof never reads as a neon success.

proof-tint.usage: The ground of a passed proof: the ProofTag pill, the proof pill in a header, the seal-match box. Opaque, so it reads the same on glass and on paint.

caution.usage: Caution status mark: ask me, pending, needs a look. Always beside words.

caution-tint.usage: Caution tag ground. Never a notice or card fill.

critical.usage: Critical status mark: failed, leaves for an outside model, no proof. Always beside words.

critical-text.usage: Critical status as text, and the inline alert line.

critical-tint.usage: Critical tag ground. Never a notice or card fill.

neutral.usage: Off, never, not used. A mark only: never for text.

destructive-text.usage: The destructive button label and destructive menu items.

badge-fill.usage: The count badge (decisions owed), with text-on-status.

surface-chart.usage: The opaque plot ground of every chart. Series are validated against it; charts never plot straight on glass.

chart-grid.usage: Recessive gridlines and the axis rule.

data-1.usage: Categorical series 1, in fixed order (never cycled). Validated for color-vision deficiency on adjacent pairs and 3:1 on surface-chart.

data-2.usage: Categorical series 2, in fixed order (never cycled). Validated for color-vision deficiency on adjacent pairs and 3:1 on surface-chart.

data-3.usage: Categorical series 3, in fixed order (never cycled). Validated for color-vision deficiency on adjacent pairs and 3:1 on surface-chart.

data-4.usage: Categorical series 4, in fixed order (never cycled). Validated for color-vision deficiency on adjacent pairs and 3:1 on surface-chart.

data-5.usage: Categorical series 5, in fixed order (never cycled). Validated for color-vision deficiency on adjacent pairs and 3:1 on surface-chart.

data-6.usage: Categorical series 6, in fixed order (never cycled). Validated for color-vision deficiency on adjacent pairs and 3:1 on surface-chart.

data-7.usage: Categorical series 7, in fixed order (never cycled). Validated for color-vision deficiency on adjacent pairs and 3:1 on surface-chart.

data-8.usage: Categorical series 8, in fixed order (never cycled). Validated for color-vision deficiency on adjacent pairs and 3:1 on surface-chart.

ink.usage: Overlay strokes and fills at an alpha: white on dark, black on light.

brand-blue.usage: The "AI" of the Near AI wordmark and the secondary lockup. Logos, illustration and brand moments; in the dark themes it is also data-1 and accent-soft. Not text on a light ground (2.9:1 on pane-opaque).

brand-sky.usage: Near AI Sky, from the near.ai/brand palette. The light steps of brand illustration (the marketing site's dithered art ramp). Logo, illustration and marketing use only; never text or controls.

brand-deep-blue.usage: Near AI Deep Blue, from the near.ai/brand palette. Mid steps of brand illustration. Illustration and marketing use only.

brand-tile.usage: The ground of the Near AI tile (app-icon lockup). Logo use only.

brand-tile-dark.usage: The tile ground of the dark app-icon appearance (macOS and iOS Icon Composer documents). App icons only.

brand-paper.usage: The "N" monogram on the color tile. Logo use only.

brand-ink.usage: The "near" wordmark in the color lockup on light grounds. Logo use only.

gateway-purple.usage: The old Trace purple: Gateway's dark accent until 2026-10-20 (NDS-22). It survives only in the old Trace mark and Gateway's Shared data series (#8a3dff dark, #7a2cf5 light). Never on controls.

shadow.note: Flat glass: one soft drop shadow for anything that floats; nothing painted inside a pane casts a shadow. The edge-classic-* shadows are the optional Classic (expressive) treatment.

shadow-float.usage: Panes, popovers, menus, node cards, the floating map overlay.

shadow-check.usage: The unchecked checkbox and radio ring (the only rim flat glass keeps).

edge-classic-pane.usage: Classic (expressive) theme only: the specular top highlight and bottom shade on a pane.

edge-classic-control.usage: Classic (expressive) theme only: a glass control's highlight, shade and contact shadow.

edge-classic-cta.usage: Classic (expressive) theme only: the primary button highlight and its accent glow (Gateway purple glow shown).

spacing.note: A 2-step scale to 16, then 20 and 24 (trace-commons s1-s10), extended on the 8 grid for web and touch layouts, plus the named layout measures every shell shares.

space-2.usage: Toolbar-group padding, icon-to-badge nudge, dense field gap (Unity 2px between fields).

space-4.usage: Label above a field, menu-row inset, note line spacing.

space-6.usage: Inline gap: dot to label, icon to label, chip padding.

space-8.usage: Gap between buttons in a bar, menu padding, list-row column gap.

space-10.usage: Gap between panes and between cards (pane-gap, card-gap).

space-12.usage: Pane padding, card padding (vertical), field horizontal padding plus 2.

space-14.usage: Card padding (horizontal), modal body vertical padding, overlay inset on a map.

space-16.usage: Inspector horizontal padding, phone side margin (M3 compact margin), sheet padding.

space-20.usage: Gap above an action bar, first-run step inset, section gap in settings.

space-24.usage: Tablet and web content margin (M3 medium+), large card padding, section gap.

space-32.usage: Web section spacing, gap between pane groups on large screens.

space-40.usage: Empty-state block spacing, hero padding on tablet.

space-64.usage: Hero and marketing section spacing (expressive only).

pane-gap.usage: Between floating panes in a window (and the window edge on web).

inline-gap.usage: Between an icon or dot and its words.

modal-inset.usage: Minimum gap between a modal and the window edge.

modal-inset-top.usage: Gap above a modal (clears the title bar and traffic lights).

dense-padding-left.usage: Dense inspector left padding (Unity Inspector: 18 left, 4 right, 8 top and bottom).

dense-indent.usage: Dense tree and inspector indent per nesting level (Unity, max 6 levels).

tree-indent.usage: Regular tree indent per level, after an 8px inset (trace-commons).

margin-expanded.usage: Page margin from 840px; panes separate with a 24px spacer.

radius.note: Flat glass radii (the baseline). Nested corners are concentric: inner radius = outer radius minus the padding between them, never less than radius-tile.

radius-pane.usage: Panes, modals, edge rail, menu-bar panel (flat; classic 16).

radius-control.usage: Fields, large tool tiles, edge-rail tiles (flat; classic 8).

radius-tile.usage: Small tiles, menu items, kebab ground, day-graph chips. The concentric floor.

radius-dense.usage: Dense controls in pro-tool panels (Unity Editor buttons and fields).

radius-window.usage: A window drawn by the app on web and Windows/Linux (the #1146 window radius).

radius-sheet.usage: Bottom sheets and side sheets on touch (top corners only; M3 extra-large).

radius-pill.usage: Buttons, wells, segments, chips, tags, badges, switches: every capsule.

size.note: Control heights and layout measures. Heights are minimums so labels grow with the system text size; touch targets never shrink below the platform floor.

target-pointer.usage: Recommended pointer hit target on macOS and desktop web (minimum 20).

target-touch-apple.usage: Touch hit target on iOS and iPadOS (minimum 28).

target-touch-android.usage: Touch hit target on Android and touch web.

target-spatial.usage: visionOS gaze-and-pinch target (centers at least 60 apart).

size-control-dense.usage: Dense desktop controls and property rows (Unity Editor 18-20).

size-control.usage: Desktop compact controls: round small button, segment, breadcrumb target.

size-control-large.usage: Desktop inline buttons, pickers, text fields, round buttons (inline size).

size-cta-small.usage: Every modal action-bar button (small bar size).

size-cta.usage: Every button in a window or sheet action bar (bar size) and the primary CTA.

size-control-touch.usage: iOS buttons, fields and rows; Android uses 40 visible inside a 48 target.

size-submit-pill.usage: The submit pill on tree rows.

size-list-row.usage: Desktop list row minimum; 44 on iOS, 56 on Android.

size-checkbox.usage: Checkbox and radio on desktop; 22 on touch inside a full-row target.

size-glyph.usage: Default glyph size in a control; 20 on touch toolbars.

size-pane-main.usage: The main (navigation) pane in a three-pane window.

size-pane-inspector.usage: The inspector pane (two thirds of the main pane).

size-rail-expanded.usage: Navigation rail, expanded minimum (max 360); replaces the navigation drawer.

size-sidebar.usage: Desktop and iPad sidebar default width.

size-modal-nav.usage: Section list in a settings modal or window.

size-popover-width.usage: Info popover, node card, tooltip maximum (tooltips max 300 in dense tools).

size-panel-width.usage: Menu-bar panel and edge-rail peek width.

size-readable-width.usage: Maximum line length container for running text (about 65 characters at body).

opacity-disabled.usage: Every disabled control, whole control. A disabled control shows no hover and explains why nearby.

opacity-row-off.usage: The tool tile of a list row that is off (the title steps to text-secondary instead).

opacity-skeleton.usage: The low point of a skeleton pulse.

opacity-series-reduced.usage: A lighter companion series beside the full-strength one.

blur.note: For shells without a native material (web, Windows, Linux, Android 12+). Native glass ignores these.

blur-pane.usage: backdrop-filter of a pane (navigation layer), under glass-veil and pane-fill.

blur-floating.usage: backdrop-filter of a popover, menu or node card.

blur-scrim.usage: The window content behind a modal scrim.

blur-bar.usage: A floating toolbar or tab bar over scrolling content (web and Android).

zIndex.note: Stacking order on web (App UI layers: main, popup, notification, tooltip).

z-floating.usage: Popovers, menus, node cards, floating toolbars.

breakpoint.note: Window widths in dp/pt/px. M3 breakpoints map to Apple size classes: compact below 600, regular from 600.

bp-medium.usage: Compact to medium: phone to small tablet; bottom bar becomes a rail.

bp-inspector.usage: A desktop window shows the inspector pane on first launch.

bp-map.usage: A desktop window shows the content (map) pane on first launch.

bp-large.usage: Expanded to large: expanded rail, three panes.

bp-xlarge.usage: Large to extra-large: wider panes, never wider running text.

motion.note: The one curve for non-spatial change; springs for anything that moves. linear() curves are the web rendering of the native springs. Durations. Nothing moves under Reduce Motion (prefers-reduced-motion): a change jumps to its end state.

duration-fast.usage: Hover and press fills, focus ring, checkbox (fast).

duration-reveal.usage: A compact pill or row expanding in place (reveal).

duration-standard.usage: Modal fade, pane show and hide, menus (standard).

duration-slide.usage: Footers and peeks sliding in, sub-list swaps (slide).

duration-slow.usage: Large-surface fades on web and Android (slow).

duration-pulse.usage: One skeleton pulse cycle (to 0.5 and back).

ease-standard.usage: The one curve for fades, fills, hover and press (trace-commons). Every non-spatial change.

ease-exit.usage: Elements leaving the screen for good (M3 emphasized accelerate, web only).

ease-linear.usage: Spinners and progress that turn at a constant rate.

spring-spatial-fast.usage: Small spatial moves: a switch knob, a selection indicator, a segment thumb (M3 standard fast spatial).

spring-spatial.usage: Default spatial moves: panes opening, sheets, popovers growing from their source (M3 standard default spatial).

spring-spatial-slow.usage: Large spatial moves: full-screen and window-level transitions (M3 standard slow spatial).

spring-effects.usage: Color, opacity and blur changes that must not overshoot (M3 standard default effects).

spring-expressive.usage: Hero moments only, one or two per product: a bouncy expressive move (M3 expressive fast spatial).

spring-ember.usage: The main-tab ember gliding between tabs (Gateway: response 0.35, damping fraction 0.85).

families.apple: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", "SF Pro Display", system-ui, sans-serif
families.web: system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Noto Sans", Ubuntu, Cantarell, sans-serif
families.android: "Roboto Flex", Roboto, "Google Sans Flex", system-ui, sans-serif
families.mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "Cascadia Mono", "Roboto Mono", Menlo, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace

micro.usage: Tag and badge words, chart tick labels.

eyebrow.usage: Uppercase labels over cards, fields and sections (tracked).

caption.usage: Sub-lines, helper text, timestamps, inline alerts.

label.usage: Control labels: buttons inline, pickers, segments, field text.

body.sample: Nothing is sent unless you say so.

body-strong.usage: Emphasised body: row titles, primary button labels, card titles.

heading.usage: Pane and screen headings, inspector headers.

display.usage: One headline per screen: onboarding, empty hero states.

number.usage: Hero figures and balances, tabular digits.

mono.usage: Paths, hashes, sizes, figures that describe what leaves the device.

tiers.name: Compact: macOS and desktop
tiers.note: The trace-commons scale, every step a macOS text style at its default size, so it follows the system text size. Dense desktop and pro tools.

tiers.name: Regular: web and Windows/Linux shells
tiers.note: Rem-based (16px root). Desktop browsers and the Tauri shells; 1rem = 16px, body 0.875rem.

tiers.name: Touch: iOS and iPadOS
tiers.note: Each step is a Dynamic Type text style at the Large (default) size; it scales xSmall to AX5 with the system.

tiers.name: Touch: Android
tiers.note: Each step is an M3 type-scale role in sp; scales with the system font size. Emphasized roles add weight only.

hero.name: Expressive: hero moments
hero.note: At most one or two per product, on marketing and empty hero states, never inside dense tools.

hero-display.usage: M3 displayLarge equivalent; web and tablet heroes only.

hero-figure.usage: A single headline figure (verified share, balance). Tabular digits.

meta.note: Parent system: trace-commons flat glass + Near AI logo kit + Apple Liquid Glass/HIG, Unity Foundations/App UI and Material 3 Expressive research. Gateway themes re-synced to trace-commons main@e2a1ad9d7 (2026-11-03); NDS-22 to NDS-49 from the owner's product sessions (research/sessions-2026-11.md). 2.0.0: the trace-light, trace-dark themes and trace-purple are renamed gateway-light, gateway-dark and gateway-purple (NDS-48).
